title: What a Recorded Memory Can and Cannot Prove
title_ja: 録音された記憶は何を証明できるのか

source_links.title: Library of Congress: Oral History Resources

fact_notes: 背景となる考え方は添付の資料で確認。本文と練習問題は新規制作。例示した人物・学校・活動は架空の説明用設定。

sentences.en: When a town prepares to celebrate its hundredth anniversary, students interview residents who remember the old shopping street.
sentences.ja: 町が百周年を祝おうとするとき、生徒たちは昔の商店街を覚えている住民に取材します。

sentences.en: One interviewee describes a busy market filled with voices, bicycles, and small family shops.
sentences.ja: ある取材対象者は声、自転車、家族経営の小店でにぎわう市場を描写します。

sentences.en: Another person, who lived nearby during the same period, remembers the street as noisy and difficult to cross.
sentences.ja: 同じ時代に近くに住んだ別の人は、その道を騒がしく渡りにくいと覚えています。

sentences.en: Both memories may be sincere even though they create very different pictures of the same place.
sentences.ja: 同じ場所の異なる姿を描いても、両方の記憶は誠実なものかもしれません。

sentences.en: Students who expect one perfect account may be tempted to label one witness correct and the other mistaken.
sentences.ja: 唯一の完璧な説明を期待する生徒は、一方を正しく他方を間違いと決めたくなるかもしれません。

sentences.en: However, oral history requires asking what each person experienced and why their perspective might differ.
sentences.ja: しかし口述歴史では各人が何を経験し、なぜ視点が異なるか尋ねる必要があります。

sentences.en: The students begin by recording the date of each interview and the questions that were asked.
sentences.ja: 生徒は各取材の日付と尋ねた質問を記録することから始めます。

sentences.en: They also ask participants for permission to preserve and share the recordings for the school project.
sentences.ja: 学校の活動のため録音を保存・共有する許可も参加者に求めます。

sentences.en: For example, someone may agree to a classroom presentation but not to making their entire voice recording publicly available.
sentences.ja: 例えば教室での発表には同意しても声の全録音を公開することは望まない人もいます。

sentences.en: The student's responsibility is not only to gather stories but to respect the conditions under which they were offered.
sentences.ja: 生徒の責任は話を集めるだけでなく、それが提供された条件を尊重することです。

sentences.en: A written transcript helps researchers search for details, yet it may not capture every pause or change in tone.
sentences.ja: 書き起こしは詳細を検索しやすくしますが、間や声の調子の変化はすべて残せないかもしれません。

sentences.en: Careful archiving records enough context that a later reader can understand what the speaker actually said.
sentences.ja: 慎重な保存では後の読み手が発言を理解できる十分な文脈を記録します。

sentences.en: The research team then compares the interviews with old photographs, maps, and newspaper reports.
sentences.ja: 調査チームは取材を古い写真、地図、新聞記事と比較します。

sentences.en: A photograph might confirm that a particular shop existed, but it does not reveal how customers felt about it.
sentences.ja: 写真は特定の店があったと確認できても、客がどう感じたかは明らかにしません。

sentences.en: In addition, a newspaper report may reflect the concerns of an editor rather than every resident's experience.
sentences.ja: さらに新聞記事は住民全員の経験より編集者の関心を反映しているかもしれません。

sentences.en: Each source has strengths and limits related to how it was produced and for whom.
sentences.ja: 各資料には作られ方と対象読者によって長所と限界があります。

sentences.en: If two records disagree, historians investigate the circumstances instead of automatically discarding one of them.
sentences.ja: 二つの記録が矛盾したら、歴史研究者はどちらかを自動的に捨てず事情を調べます。

sentences.en: A contradiction can be an opportunity to learn whose interests or experiences were previously overlooked.
sentences.ja: 矛盾は以前見逃された人の利害や経験を学ぶ機会にもなります。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, understanding perspectives should not mean accepting every remembered detail as an established fact.
sentences.ja: それでも視点を理解することは思い出されたすべての細部を確定事実とすることではありません。

sentences.en: A witness may remember a shop at the wrong corner or confuse two events that happened years apart.
sentences.ja: 証言者は店の角を取り違えたり数年離れた出来事を混同したりするかもしれません。

sentences.en: Researchers can state clearly which claims have independent support and which remain uncertain.
sentences.ja: 研究者は独立した裏づけがある主張と不確かな主張を明確に示せます。

sentences.en: The goal is not to embarrass an interviewee but to produce an accurate and respectful account of the past.
sentences.ja: 目的は取材対象者に恥をかかせることではなく、正確で敬意ある過去の記述を作ることです。

sentences.en: When historians explain the limitations of their sources, readers can judge the strength of the conclusions.
sentences.ja: 歴史研究者が資料の限界を説明すれば読み手は結論の強さを判断できます。

sentences.en: A responsible project therefore makes room for both personal memory and evidence that can be checked.
sentences.ja: 責任ある活動では個人の記憶と確認できる証拠の両方に場所を与えます。

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Oral memories should always be rejected.
Oral history is useful when memories are documented, compared, and interpreted carefully.
Photographs are more important than all testimony.
Every witness must remember identical details.
questions.explanation_ja: 証言の価値を尊重しつつ他の証拠と照合することが主題です。

questions.prompt: How do the two interviewees remember the street differently?
options: One remembers trains and the other buses.
One remembers a school and the other a hospital.
One recalls a lively market while the other remembers noise and danger.
Both give exactly the same description.
questions.explanation_ja: 活気と騒音・通行困難という異なる視点です。

questions.prompt: Why might both memories be sincere?
options: People can experience the same place from different perspectives.
Only one person actually lived nearby.
questions.explanation_ja: 同じ出来事でも立場によって感じ方が違うからです。

questions.prompt: What permission might participants choose to give?
options: Only permission to change the past.
Only permission to write a fictional story.
Permission for classroom use but not public audio release.
questions.explanation_ja: 教室利用のみ同意し公開は望まない例です。

questions.prompt: What may a transcript fail to capture?
options: Pauses and changes in vocal tone.
questions.explanation_ja: 書き起こしでは間や声の変化が消え得ます。

questions.prompt: Why is a newspaper not an entirely neutral account?
options: Editors can never change an article.
Its content may reflect editorial priorities and limited perspectives.
Every resident is interviewed for every report.
questions.explanation_ja: 編集者の関心が反映されることがあるためです。

options: A disagreement between accounts or pieces of evidence.
A written agreement to share information.

questions.prompt: What should researchers do when evidence is uncertain?
options: Identify which claims are supported and which remain unverified.
questions.explanation_ja: 確認できる主張と未確認の主張を区別します。

questions.prompt: Why is criticism of a mistaken detail not meant to embarrass an interviewee?
options: The aim is respectful historical accuracy, not personal blame.
A researcher should avoid asking questions.
questions.explanation_ja: 正確さと敬意を両立する目的だからです。

options: One perfect source can explain the past.
Memories matter only when recorded in video.
Personal testimony and independently checkable evidence both have a role.
questions.explanation_ja: 記憶と検証可能な証拠を両立する結論です。
